reports.title: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE) Guatemala
reports.description: Guatemala's national statistics office, responsible for the population and housing census, household and price surveys, and coordination of the national statistical system (SEN).

reports.title: Cuentas Nacionales de Guatemala (SCN 2008, año de referencia 2013)
reports.description: Guatemala's official national accounts compilation, produced by the central bank, covering GDP by production, expenditure and institutional-sector accounts on a 2013 reference year.

reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) Guatemala — cambio de año base (CCIF 2018)
reports.description: Guatemala's official monthly consumer price index, updated with a 2024 methodology and base-year change adopting CCIF/COICOP 2018 and the IMF's 2020 CPI Concepts and Methods Manual.

reports.title: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE) Honduras
reports.description: Honduras's national statistics office, responsible for censuses, household surveys and coordination of the national statistical system.

reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) Honduras — base diciembre 2025=100
reports.description: Honduras's official monthly consumer price index, rebased to December 2025=100 with 405 products classified under COICOP 2018 (13 divisions) and the IMF's 2020 CPI Concepts and Methods Manual.

reports.title: Instituto Nacional de Información de Desarrollo (INIDE)
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Información de Desarrollo
reports.description: Nicaragua's national statistics institute, responsible for censuses, household surveys, the consumer price index and coordination of the national statistical system; the site continues to publish monthly inflation and other releases as of mid-2026, though the country's IMF data-dissemination metadata has not been meaningfully updated in some years.

reports.title: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INEC) Costa Rica
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos
reports.description: Costa Rica's national statistics and census institute, an autonomous government body responsible for the census, household surveys, the CPI and coordination of the National Statistical System (SEN); the country's national accounts are compiled separately by the central bank.

reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) Costa Rica
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos
reports.description: Costa Rica's official monthly consumer price index, compiled by INEC using COICOP 2018 classification and following the IMF's CPI Manual (2004 and 2020 editions).

reports.title: Cuentas Nacionales de Costa Rica
reports.description: Costa Rica's official national accounts (GDP) compilation, produced by the central bank on a 2017 reference year under the System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008).

reports.title: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censo (INEC) Panama
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censo, Contraloría General de la República
reports.description: Panama's national statistics and census institute, operating under the Comptroller General's Office; compiles national accounts, CPI, balance of payments and other macroeconomic statistics.

reports.title: Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales de Panamá — Año de referencia 2018
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censo
reports.description: Panama's official national accounts series with a 2018 reference year, compiled under System of National Accounts 2008 (SCN 2008) recommendations with chain-linked volume measures and a homogeneous 1996-2024 historical series.

reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) Panama — base 2024=100
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censo
reports.description: Panama's official monthly consumer price index, rebased to 2024=100 with 343 articles classified under CCIF/COICOP 2018 (13 divisions).

reports.title: Balanza de Pagos de Panamá
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censo — Sección de Balanza de Pagos, Departamento de Estadísticas Económicas
reports.description: Panama's official balance-of-payments statistics, compiled by INEC's Balance of Payments Section under the sixth edition of the IMF's Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual (BPM6).

reports.title: Statistical Institute of Belize (SIB)
reports.description: Belize's national statistical institute, responsible for national accounts, CPI, censuses and household surveys.

reports.title: Comisión Centroamericana de Estadística (CENTROESTAD) — SICA
reports.description: SICA's regional statistical commission, bringing together the heads of Central American and Dominican Republic national statistics offices to coordinate statistical harmonisation, training and regional comparability; member offices rotate its six-month pro-tempore presidency.

reports.title: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Good Statistical Practice (OECD/LEGAL/0417)
reports.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
reports.description: The OECD's sole legal instrument on statistics, adopted by the Council on 23 November 2015, setting twelve recommendations on institutional frameworks, methodology, quality assurance and coordination for national statistical systems; used as a benchmark in Costa Rica's OECD accession statistical review.

dependencies.basis: Banco de Guatemala's own conceptual/methodological document for the 2013-reference-year national accounts states adoption of SCN 2008 as the compilation framework: “se adoptó el Sistema Cuentas Nacionales 2008 (SCN 2008) como marco metodológico de compilación.”

The IMF's own dated press release documents Guatemala's upgrade to the enhanced dissemination tier, after first joining the original GDDS in December 2004: “Guatemala Implements the International Monetary Fund's Enhanced General Data Dissemination System” (18 November 2020).

INE Guatemala's own news post on its 2024 CENTROESTAD regional forum participation identifies the body directly as “the Central American Statistical Commission of SICA,” and Guatemala's government press service separately reports INE holding CENTROESTAD's pro-tempore presidency.

INE's own base-change methodology document states the 2018 edition of CCIF/COICOP was implemented to code the CPI basket: “La implementación de la Clasificación del Consumo Individual por Finalidades (CCIF) versión 2018 para la codificación de los bienes y servicios de la canasta que conforma el IPC.”

The same INE document cites the IMF's 2020 CPI manual as the source of its methodology changes: “Los principales cambios se realizan con base a recomendaciones del Manual de Métodos y Conceptos del IPC 2020.”

Banco Central de Honduras's own methodology note for the new December-2025=100 base states the 2018 UN classification is used: “la Clasificación del Consumo Individual por Finalidades (CCIF) de la Organización de las Naciones Unidas (ONU) 2018, que divide estrictamente los bienes y servicios en trece grupos.”

The same BCH note cites the IMF's 2020 CPI Concepts and Methods Manual as its governing methodological reference: “recomendaciones metodológicas establecidas en el Manual de Conceptos y Métodos del IPC (2020).”

The IMF's own DSBB annual report for Costa Rica confirms SDDS (not SDDS Plus) subscription: “Costa Rica subscribed to the SDDS on November 28, 2001, and met all the SDDS requirements at the time of subscription.”

OECD's own statistical-system accession review of Costa Rica (mirrored on INEC's own SEN portal) states Costa Rica adhered to the Recommendation without conditions: “Costa Rica accepted it with no reservations, observations or timeframes for implementation,” tying this to the 2019 Statistics Act (Law No. 9694) governing INEC and the national statistical system.

INEC's own 2023 annual report (Memoria) lists follow-up on CENTROESTAD agreements among its international-cooperation activities: “seguimiento a acuerdos regionales en el marco de Centroestad y CEA-CEPAL.”

Costa Rica's SDDS metadata for the CPI category states the classification used is the current COICOP edition: “The classification system used for the CPI is the original version of the most recent COICOP (COICOP 2018).”

The same SDDS metadata states the CPI is based on both editions of the CPI manual: “The CPI is based on the Consumer Price Index Manual: Theory and Practice (2004) and on the Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods (2020).”

BCCR's own national-accounts reference-year-2017 summary states the update was carried out under SNA 2008: “La actualización fue ejecutada en el marco metodológico del Manual del Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales 2008 (SNA2008).”
The IMF's own dated press release documents Panama's enhanced-tier participation: “Panama Implements the IMF's Enhanced General Data Dissemination System” (10 October 2018).

INEC's own methodology note for the homogeneous 1996-2024 series states the recommendations of SCN 2008 were incorporated: “incorporando las recomendaciones metodológicas del Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales 2008 (SCN2008).”

INEC's own technical note for the 2024=100 CPI base states the CCIF 2018 classification is used, organised in 13 divisions: “La canasta del IPC base 2024=100 utiliza la Clasificación del Consumo Individual por Finalidades (CCIF 2018)... Los artículos y servicios se ordenan en 13 divisiones.”

INEC's own Balance-of-Payments Section methodology note states the sixth edition of the manual was adopted: “con la adopción de metodologías recomendadas, a nivel internacional, por la sexta edición del Manual de Balanza de Pagos y Posición de Inversión Internacional.”

SIB's own 2022 rebasing documentation describes the transition to the new standard, including FISIM and capitalisation-of-intellectual-property treatment changes it required: “The transition from SNA 1993 to SNA 2008” and “following the SNA 2008, it recommends for the capitalization of intellectual property products such as, oil exploration, research and development and software development.”

SIB's own July 2026 news post confirms Belize's membership and its rotating leadership of the body: “CENTROESTAD is the statistical Commission of the Central American Integration System (SICA)” and that SIB “will serve as the Pro Tempore President of the Central American Statistical Commission (CENTROESTAD) from July to December 2026.”

_dropped.why: [MISQUOTE] Grok's quote ("...consistent with the 2008 System of National Accounts (2008 SNA)") does not match the live DSBB e-GDDS CPI00 page for Honduras (https://dsbb.imf.org/e-gdds/dqaf-base/country/HND/category/CPI00, fetched via the JSON API since the rendered page is a JS shell), which actually states 'The definition of expenditure of ENIGH households is consistent with the 1993 System of National Accounts (SNA93).' Separately, that DSBB page describes the OLD CPI base (December 1999=100, sourced from a 1998-99 ENIGH survey) -- a different vintage from the proposed hn-bch-cpi-2025 (base December 2025=100) -- so even a corrected edition would be targeting the wrong report. 'sna-1993' is also not currently a live corpus id, so it isn't mintable as a target without separately proposing that node, which felt out of scope for a single stale citation. Flagging for a human: a genuine SNA93 dependency likely exists for Honduras's legacy (pre-2025) CPI series, but not for the new Dec-2025 base.

[GENERIC-QUOTE] Grok's cited SECMCA press release only states that a CPI technical-group meeting included representatives of 'Bancos Centrales y Oficinas Nacionales de Estadistica de los paises miembros del SICA' generically -- Honduras is never named specifically. Could not find an ine.gob.hn page or other Honduras-specific primary source confirming its own CENTROESTAD/SICA participation, unlike Guatemala, Belize and Costa Rica, where each NSO's own site names its participation directly.

[GENERIC-QUOTE / UNREACHABLE SOURCE] Grok's evidence is SICA's own generic si-ESTAD landing page, which describes the regional system in general terms with no Panama-specific statement; sica.int also returned a 403 on every live-fetch attempt in this pass, so even the generic page could not be independently confirmed. Could not find an inec.gob.pa page or other Panama-specific primary source confirming CENTROESTAD participation (contrast with the Guatemala/Belize/Costa Rica edges above, each sourced from that country's own NSO domain).

[WRONG AGENCY] Costa Rica's national accounts (GDP) are compiled and published by the Banco Central de Costa Rica (BCCR), not INEC -- confirmed via BCCR's own 'Cuentas Nacionales Referencia 2017' document, which independently reproduces the same SNA2008 statement Grok found. Re-sourced as a new report node (cr-bccr-national-accounts -> sna-2008, included above) rather than attaching the edge to the INEC institutional node, which does not itself compile this release.

[WRONG NODE LEVEL / CONTAINMENT] The BPM6 adoption itself is real and independently verified (INEC's own 'Nota metodologica VI Manual de Balanza de Pagos (MBP6)' document), but pa-inec is the general institutional node for the whole statistics office, not the specific Balance-of-Payments release -- attaching a release-specific methodology standard there doesn't match how the rest of the corpus models this (id-bop, iq-bop, ph-bop etc. are all separate report nodes). Minted a dedicated pa-inec-balance-of-payments report node instead and attached the edge there.

[JS-WALLED / WRONG NODE LEVEL] Grok's evidence_url (dsbb.imf.org/e-gdds/important-dates-history) is a client-rendered DSBB page that returns no country-specific content on live fetch (via WebFetch or the DSBB JSON API pattern) -- Grok's quoted per-country date-table entry for Guatemala could not be independently confirmed. Separately, e-GDDS participation is a country-wide dissemination-tier status, not something specific to one national-accounts release. Re-sourced and re-attached as gt-ine -> imf-e-gdds (included above) using two independently confirmable IMF press releases instead.

[JS-WALLED, considered on my own initiative -- not a Grok claim] Looked for an IMF press release analogous to Guatemala's or Panama's confirming Honduras's e-GDDS implementation and found none; DSBB's own e-GDDS country/status pages (e.g. dsbb.imf.org/egdds/country/HND/category) are client-rendered and returned no participation-status text on live fetch. The URL path segment on Honduras's CPI DQAF page (.../e-gdds/dqaf-base/country/HND/category/CPI00) implies e-GDDS classification, and its body content did independently confirm real, Honduras-specific detail (Central Bank of Honduras, ENIGH-based weights) -- but that falls short of an explicit statement of Honduras's dissemination-tier status, so left unminted rather than inferred from a URL path alone.

[NI THIN, BUT INSTITUTE ITSELF CONFIRMED CURRENT] INIDE's own site is genuinely live and current -- it is publishing monthly inflation notes as of June 2026 ('Nota de Prensa de Inflacion junio 2026'), so the institutional node above is solid. But Nicaragua's IMF/DSBB metadata (checked live via the JSON API for NIC/CPI00 and NIC/NAG00) is stale: the CPI page describes a base-1999=100 index compiled by the Central Bank of Nicaragua (not INIDE) from a 1998-99 household survey with no COICOP edition stated, and the national-accounts page still describes SNA93 methodology with a 1994 reference year. The IMF's 2022 Article IV report (Country Report 23/53) independently states 'the timeliness and frequency of certain published reports have deteriorated since 2018.' None of this supports a current, edition-specific methodology edge -- consistent with Grok's own thin/null call for Nicaragua. Flagging as a lead only, in case INIDE's own current inflation release yields a fresh, citable methodology statement in a later pass.

[CONFIRMS GROK'S OWN THIN CALL] Independently checked Belize's DSBB CPI metadata live (JSON API for BLZ/CPI00): it references COICOP only at 'the four-digit level' with no edition/year stated, and is built on a 1990 Household Budget Survey -- too old and unspecific to support a un-coicop-2018 (or any edition) edge. Grok correctly declined to propose a Belize CPI methodology edge in either batch; this just confirms that call rather than adding a new one.
